    for x in a:

    return p

print(p[3] - p[1])  # 10

title: Variables & types
lesson: Python names refer to objects. Integers, floats, strings and booleans represent different kinds of values. Convert explicitly when reading numeric text.
code:
age = int("30")
print(age + 1)  # 31

title: Conditions & loops
lesson: Use if to choose a branch and for to visit a sequence. range(n) yields 0 through n-1. Track a variable whose meaning stays clear after every iteration.
question: Which values are in range(3)?

title: Functions & scope
lesson: Functions isolate reusable work. return sends a value to the caller; print only displays it. Prefer parameters over changing global state.
question: Which sends a result to the caller?
task: Write a function clamp(x, low, high) that returns x restricted to the inclusive bounds. Example: clamp(12,0,10) → 10.

title: Dictionaries & counting
lesson: A dictionary maps keys to values. get(key, default) helps count new keys without a separate branch. Dictionary lookup is average constant time.
question: What does get("new", 0) return for a missing key?
complexity: O(n) average time, O(u) distinct keys

title: Exceptions & input validation
lesson: Raise an exception when a function receives invalid input. Catch specific expected exceptions at a boundary where you can recover; avoid hiding unexpected errors.

title: Strings & character counts
lesson: Strings are immutable sequences. Count characters with a map. State whether comparison is case-sensitive and whether spaces count.

title: Stacks & brackets
lesson: A stack follows last in, first out. For balanced brackets, push opening brackets and match each closing bracket to the latest opening bracket.
code:

stack.append("(")
print(stack.pop())  # (

complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for bracket matching

q.append("next")

title: Linked lists & pointers
lesson: A linked list stores nodes connected by references. Save the next reference before reversing a link, or you can lose the rest of the list.
code:
def reverse(head):
    previous = None
    while head:
        following = head.next
        head.next = previous
        previous, head = head, following
    return previous

title: Digits & integer arithmetic
lesson: Extract a nonnegative integer’s last digit with n % 10. Remove it with n // 10. Handle zero explicitly when counting digits.
code:
def digit_sum(n):
    n = abs(n)
    total = 0
    while n:
        total += n % 10
        n //= 10
    return total

lesson: The greatest common divisor satisfies gcd(a,b) = gcd(b,a % b). Repeatedly reduce until the second value is zero. Normalize signs first.

title: Prime numbers
lesson: A prime has exactly two positive divisors. If n is composite, at least one factor is at most its square root. Values below two are not prime.
question: Is 1 prime?

title: Probability & conditional events
lesson: Conditional probability changes the sample space: P(A given B) = P(A and B) / P(B), provided P(B) > 0. Independence is an assumption you must justify.
question: P(A and B)=0.2, P(B)=0.5. P(A given B)?

title: Vectors & dot products
lesson: The dot product sums pairwise products of equal-length vectors. In a linear model, it combines features and weights before adding a bias.
question: Dot product of [1,2] and [3,4]?

title: Derivatives & optimization
lesson: A derivative measures local rate of change. Gradient descent moves opposite the gradient to reduce a smooth objective, with a suitable learning rate.
code:

learning_rate = 0.1
for _ in range(20):
    gradient = 2*x  # derivative of x squared
    x -= learning_rate * gradient

lesson: Fit parameters on training data. Use validation data for model selection. Keep the test set untouched until final evaluation. Split related records together to prevent leakage.

title: Regression & squared error
lesson: Regression predicts continuous targets. Mean squared error averages squared residuals and penalizes large errors strongly. Compare against a simple baseline.

title: Classification metrics
lesson: Precision asks how many predicted positives were correct. Recall asks how many actual positives were found. F1 is their harmonic mean. Accuracy can mislead on imbalanced labels.
code:
def precision_recall(tp, fp, fn):
    precision = tp/(tp+fp) if tp+fp else 0.0
    recall = tp/(tp+fn) if tp+fn else 0.0
    return precision, recall

lesson: Embeddings represent items as numeric vectors. Cosine similarity compares direction; it is undefined for a zero-length vector. Similarity depends on the model and is not proof of truth.

lesson: Tests document observable behavior. Include typical inputs, boundary cases and invalid inputs. A passing test suite increases confidence but cannot prove the absence of all bugs.

lesson: SQL groups related rows and aggregates values. WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation. Use parameterized queries for untrusted values.
